1.word_for_word: pañca-catvāriṃśake — in the forty-fifth chapter; pitṛ-nanda-ādi-sāntvanam — consoling the parents, Nanda and others; ugrasena-abhiṣekaḥ — coronation of Ugrasena; gurau vāsāt pura-āgamaḥ — return to the city after residence with the guru; upalabdha-arthau viditvā — seeing that the parents had attained the understanding; āvām īśvarau iti — ‘these two are Lords’; parama-jñāna-rūpaḥ arthaḥ labdhaḥ — the highest knowledge had been attained; mayi prasanne anayoḥ jñānam kim durlabham — with me pleased, what knowledge could be difficult for them?; durlabham tu mayi putratayā prema — what is rare is love for me as their son; idānīm tat jñānam mā bhūt — let that knowledge now recede; nijām svādhīnām māyām tayoḥ prasāritavān — he extended his own controlled māyā over them
1.translation: The forty-fifth chapter describes the consolation of Kṛṣṇa's parents, Nanda and the others, Ugrasena's coronation, the brothers' residence with their guru and their return to the city. Kṛṣṇa saw that Vasudeva and Devakī had already attained the exalted understanding that the two boys were the Supreme Lords before they had enjoyed the ordinary supreme happiness of regarding them simply as sons standing nearby. If Kṛṣṇa is pleased, such knowledge is not difficult to obtain; what is truly rare is parental love that sees him as one's own son. Therefore Kṛṣṇa now caused that awareness of his divinity to recede and extended over them his own māyā, which is completely under his control.

2.word_for_word: tad eva darśayati — the following passage shows this; uvāca-ādi aṣṭabhiḥ — through eight verses beginning with ‘he said’; prīṇan — delighting them; prīṇayan — causing them pleasure; sa-ārdaram bruvan — speaking with tenderness
2.translation: The next eight verses beginning with ‘he said’ show this change. Kṛṣṇa speaks tenderly and affectionately, delighting his parents.

3.word_for_word: asmat-nimittam — because of us; nityam utkaṇṭhitayoḥ api yuvayoḥ — although you two always longed for us; putrābhyām āvābhyām kṛtvā — through us, your sons; bālya-paugaṇḍa-kaiśora-avasthā-anubhava-sukhāni — joys of experiencing childhood, boyhood and adolescence; na abhavan — did not occur
3.translation: Because of what happened to us, although you always longed for your sons, you were deprived of the joys that parents normally experience as their children pass through infancy, boyhood and adolescence.

4.word_for_word: āvām eva daiva-hīnau — we ourselves were deprived by fate; pitṛ-geha-sthā bālāḥ yām mudam vindante — the happiness children experience while living in their parents' home; sā na labdhā — that too we did not obtain
4.translation: Kṛṣṇa adds that the loss was mutual: ‘We too were deprived by fate, for we did not obtain the happiness children ordinarily experience while growing up in their parents' home.’

5.word_for_word: yuvayoḥ āvayoḥ ca kāma-hāniḥ — both your longing and ours went unfulfilled; yuṣmat-paricaryā-lopena dharma-hāniḥ api — by failing to serve you we also suffered a loss of duty; sarvārtha-sambhavaḥ dehaḥ — the body in which all aims of life arise; yābhyām janitaḥ poṣitaḥ ca — generated and nourished by the parents; tayoḥ pitroḥ nirveśam niṣkṛtim ānṛṇyam — repayment, requital, freedom from debt to those parents; martyaḥ śata-saṃvatsara-mātreṇa āyuṣā na prāpnoti — a mortal cannot attain it even in a hundred-year life
5.translation: The previous two verses show that both parents and sons were deprived of their desired happiness. Kṛṣṇa now says that he and Balarāma also suffered a loss of dharma because they could not serve their parents. The body in which all human aims—dharma and the rest—can be pursued is generated and nourished by one's parents. A mortal cannot fully repay that debt, even with an entire hundred-year lifespan.

6.word_for_word: putraḥ kalpaḥ samarthaḥ san api — a son who is competent and capable; ātmanā dehena dhanena ca — with his own body and wealth; pitroḥ vṛttim jīvikām na sampādayet — does not provide his parents' livelihood; pretya lokāntare — after death in another world; yama-dūtāḥ — Yama's messengers; svasya eva māṃsam khādayanti — make him eat his own flesh
6.translation: A son who is fully capable yet refuses to support his parents with his body, labor and wealth is punished after death: Yama's messengers make him consume his own flesh.

7.word_for_word: mātṛ-ādi-śuśrūṣām akurvan — failing to serve mother and the others who deserve care; viphalajīvitaḥ — living a fruitless life; abibhrat — not maintaining them; apoṣṇan — not nourishing them; śvasan api mṛta-tulyaḥ — although breathing, equal to a dead man
7.translation: One who fails to care for his mother and the other dependents whom he is obliged to maintain lives a fruitless life. Even though he still breathes, one who does not support and nourish them is effectively as good as dead.

8.word_for_word: tat tasmāt — therefore; nau āvayoḥ — of us two; mogham — vain; vyartham — wasted; anarcatoḥ — because we did not worship; apūjayatoḥ — because we did not honor you
8.translation: ‘Therefore our lives have in that respect been vain and wasted, because we were unable to worship and honor you as sons ought to honor their parents.’

9.word_for_word: durhṛdā kaṃsena kṛtvā — because of the evil-hearted Kaṃsa
9.translation: All of this separation and deprivation occurred because of the evil-hearted Kaṃsa.

13.word_for_word: tvam eva ājñāpaya iti mā vada — do not say, ‘You yourself should rule’; yayāti-śāpāt — because of Yayāti's curse; tava tu yādavatve api — although you too are a Yādava; mat-ājñayā na doṣaḥ — there is no fault when acting by my command
13.translation: Kṛṣṇa forestalls Ugrasena's possible reply, ‘You yourself should rule.’ Because of Yayāti's curse the Yadus do not ordinarily assume kingship, but although Ugrasena is a Yādava, there is no fault in his ruling when it is done by Kṛṣṇa's command.

14.word_for_word: mama tādṛśī śaktiḥ na asti iti cet — if he says ‘I do not possess such power’; mayi iti — the verse beginning ‘in me’; mat-prasādena sarvam bhaviṣyati — everything will be accomplished by my grace
14.translation: If Ugrasena objects, ‘I do not possess the power required to rule,’ Kṛṣṇa answers that by his grace everything necessary will be accomplished.

15.word_for_word: svān jñātīn sambandhān ca — their own relatives and connections; digbhyaḥ ānāyya — bringing them back from all directions
15.translation: They had their relatives and family connections brought back from every direction.

17.word_for_word: siddhāḥ — fulfilled, perfected; pūrṇāḥ — complete; kṛṣṇa-rāmābhyām gataḥ nivṛttaḥ jvaraḥ tāpaḥ yeṣām — whose fever and distress had been removed by Kṛṣṇa and Rāma
17.translation: They became ‘siddha,’ fulfilled and complete: the fever of their distress had been removed by Kṛṣṇa and Rāma.

18.word_for_word: sa-daya-smitam vīkṣaṇam — a glance accompanied by a compassionate smile
18.translation: His glance was accompanied by a tender, compassionate smile.

19.word_for_word: pravayasaḥ — advanced in age; vṛddhāḥ api — although elderly; atiśayitam balam ojaḥ ca yeṣām — possessing extraordinary strength and vigor
19.translation: Although advanced in age, they possessed extraordinary strength and vigor.

21.word_for_word: bhṛśam ātmano api ādhikyena poṣitau — nourished them intensely, even more carefully than themselves; na ca āścaryam — this is not surprising; ātmano dehāt api ātmajeṣu abhyadhikā prītiḥ — affection for one's children is greater even than affection for one's own body
21.translation: Nanda and Yaśodā had nourished the two boys with even greater care than they gave themselves. This is not surprising: love for one's children is naturally stronger even than attachment to one's own body.

22.word_for_word: devakī-vasudevayoḥ putrau yuvām — you two are the sons of Devakī and Vasudeva; na asmat-putrau iti api na vācyam — it should not therefore be said that you are not our sons; sa pitā iti — this is answered by the statement ‘he is the father...’
22.translation: Nor should one say to Nanda and Yaśodā, ‘You are not their parents because the boys are the sons of Devakī and Vasudeva.’ The verse beginning ‘He is the father…’ establishes parenthood also through nurturing, protection and affection.

24.word_for_word: sa-vrajam — together with Vraja; vraja-vāsibhiḥ sahitam — together with all the residents of Vraja; kupyāni — valuables other than gold and silver; svarṇa-rajata-ādi-vyatirikta — excluding gold, silver and the like; kāṃsya-pātra-ādīni — bronze vessels and similar goods
24.translation: ‘Together with Vraja’ means together with all the residents of Vraja. The ‘kupya’ goods were valuable household articles distinct from gold and silver, such as bronze vessels and similar property.

26.word_for_word: purodhasā gargācāryeṇa — by the family priest Garga Ācārya; dvija-saṃskṛtim — the rite making one twice-born; upanayanam — initiation with the sacred thread
26.translation: Their family priest Garga Ācārya performed their upanayana, the initiation rite by which a boy enters the status of a twice-born student.

27.word_for_word: gāvaḥ — cows; rukma-mālā vidyante yāsām — adorned with golden garlands; kṣauma-vastra-mālāvatīḥ — decorated with linen cloth and garlands
27.translation: The cows given in charity were richly adorned, with golden ornaments or garlands and with fine linen cloth and floral decorations.

28.word_for_word: yāḥ pūrvam mano-dattāḥ āsan — the very cows previously promised mentally; tāḥ eva adadāt — he gave those same cows; kamsena apahṛtāḥ — they had been seized by Kaṃsa; satyam — true; rāja-goṣṭhāt ācchidya dattāḥ — Vasudeva recovered them from the royal herd and then donated them
28.translation: Vasudeva now gave the very cows that he had previously resolved in his mind to donate. One may object that Kaṃsa had confiscated those cows. True: after Kaṃsa's fall Vasudeva recovered them from the royal herd and then completed the intended gift.

29.word_for_word: gāyatram vratam — the vow associated with the Gāyatrī; brahmacaryam — life of a celibate Vedic student
29.translation: The ‘Gāyatra vow’ is the discipline of brahmacarya undertaken by the initiated Vedic student.

30-31.word_for_word: prakarṣeṇa bhavanti ābhyām iti prabhavau — they are ‘prabhavau’ because things arise powerfully from these two; ata eva sarvajñau — hence they are omniscient; svataḥ-siddham amalam jñānam — naturally perfect and stainless knowledge; nara-ceṣṭitaiḥ pracchādayantau — concealing it beneath human-like activities
30-31.translation: The brothers are called ‘prabhavau’ because all powers and manifestations arise from them; therefore they are inherently omniscient. Their knowledge is naturally perfect and stainless, but in their human-like līlā they concealed that knowledge beneath the behavior of ordinary young men.

32.word_for_word: yathā — duly, properly; upasādya prāpya — approaching and reaching the guru; gurau vṛttim — proper conduct toward the teacher; anyān grāhayantau śikṣayantau — teaching others by their example; gurum upetau — they went to the guru; sevitavantau — they served him
32.translation: They approached the guru in the proper manner and observed the conduct required toward him, thereby teaching others by their own example. ‘They went to the guru’ means that they entered his service as students.

33.word_for_word: śuddhaḥ bhāvaḥ yāsu tābhiḥ anuvṛttibhiḥ — through acts of service performed with pure intention; sa-aṅga-upaniṣadaḥ — the Vedas together with their limbs and Upaniṣads; aṅgāni ṣaḍ-aṅgāni śikṣā-ādīni — the six Vedāṅgas beginning with phonetics; upaniṣadbhiḥ ca sahitān — together with the Upaniṣads
33.translation: They served their teacher with acts of attendance motivated by a pure disposition. From him they studied the Vedas together with their six limbs beginning with śikṣā and with the Upaniṣads.

34.word_for_word: sa-rahasyam — together with its secret teaching; mantra-devatā-jñāna-sahitam — including knowledge of mantra and its deity; dharmān — Dharmaśāstras; manu-ādi-dharma-śāstrāṇi — codes beginning with Manu; nyāya-pathān — systems of disciplined reasoning and interpretation; mīmāṃsā-ādīn — beginning with Mīmāṃsā; ānvīkṣikīm — analytical philosophy; tarka-vidyām — science of reasoning; ṣaḍ-vidhām rāja-nītim — sixfold political science; sandhiḥ — treaty or peace; vigrahaḥ — hostility or war; yānam — marching; āsanam — remaining in place; dvaidham — divided policy; āśrayaḥ — seeking protection or alliance
34.translation: They learned sacred lore together with its esoteric knowledge of mantras and their deities, the Dharmaśāstras beginning with Manu, paths of interpretation such as Mīmāṃsā, and ānvīkṣikī, the discipline of logic and reasoning. They also learned the sixfold science of statecraft: making peace, engaging in war, marching against an enemy, remaining in position, pursuing a divided or dual policy, and seeking the protection or alliance of another power.

35.word_for_word: sakṛt nigada-mātreṇa — merely from a single recitation; eka-vāram guroḥ uccāraṇa-mātreṇa — after the guru uttered it only once; catuḥ-ṣaṣṭi-kalāḥ — the sixty-four arts
35.translation: The brothers mastered each discipline after hearing the guru state it only once. Śrīdhara then gives the traditional list of sixty-four arts: (1) singing; (2) instrumental music; (3) dancing; (4) dramatic performance; (5) painting and drawing; (6) decorative cutting and design; (7) making ritual and ornamental designs with rice and flowers; (8) arranging beds or carpets of flowers; (9) coloring the teeth, garments and body; (10) making gem-inlaid floors and mosaics; (11) arranging beds and couches; (12) music and play performed with water; (13) pictorial composition and visual designs; (14) making and varying garlands; (15) arranging crowns and headdresses; (16) costume and stage dressing; (17) forming leaf ornaments for the ears; (18) preparing perfumes; (19) arranging ornaments; (20) magic and illusion; (21) techniques of cosmetic beautification; (22) sleight of hand; (23) preparing varied vegetables, cakes and foods; (24) preparing drinks, syrups, flavored liquids and fermented beverages; (25) needlework and weaving; (26) string games; (27) playing instruments such as the vīṇā and ḍamaru; (28) riddles; (29) verse-linking and chain recitation; (30) difficult or cryptic expressions; (31) reading books; (32) understanding and presenting dramas and narratives; (33) completing incomplete poetic compositions; (34) crafting articles from strips, cane and similar materials; (35) the transmitted art called tarka-karman; (36) carpentry; (37) architecture; (38) testing silver and precious stones; (39) metallurgy and alchemical operations; (40) knowledge of coloring and treating gems; (41) knowledge of mines and mineral deposits; (42) tree medicine and horticulture; (43) arranging contests of rams, cocks and quail; (44) teaching parrots and mynah birds to speak; (45) massage and bodily cleansing; (46) skill in grooming hair; (47) communicating letters by finger and hand signs; (48) coded, foreign or cryptic modes of speech; (49) knowledge of regional languages; (50) making flower carts and similar constructions; (51) knowledge of mechanical devices and mnemonic diagrams, as the transmitted wording indicates; (52) recitation and verbal communication; (53) composing poetry mentally; (54) lexicography; (55) knowledge of meter; (56) variants of procedures and techniques; (57) tricks and deceptive devices; (58) concealing garments and objects; (59) special forms of dice and gaming; (60) games of attraction and drawing objects; (61) children's games and toys; (62) arts of discipline and etiquette; (63) arts of victory; and (64) the arts of bards and heralds.

36.word_for_word: chandayām āsatuḥ — they invited him to choose; upalobhitavantau — induced him to state what he desired
36.translation: They invited their teacher to name the guru-dakṣiṇā he desired.

37.word_for_word: prabhāse kṣetre — at the holy place Prabhāsa; mahārṇave — in the great ocean; mṛtam bālam — the son who had died; varayām āsa — he requested him as the fee
37.translation: Their guru requested the return of his son, who had died in the great ocean at the sacred place Prabhāsa.

38.word_for_word: īśvarau iti viditvā — knowing them to be the two Lords; samudraḥ — the Ocean; tayoḥ arhaṇam ājahāra — brought them offerings of honor
38.translation: The Ocean recognized Rāma and Kṛṣṇa as the Lords and presented them with the honors due to them.

40.word_for_word: pañcajanaḥ tu asuraḥ ahārṣīt — the demon Pañcajana carried him away; sa ca mahān — he is powerful; mama asādhyaḥ — beyond my ability to subdue
40.translation: The Ocean explains: ‘The demon Pañcajana carried the boy away. He is very powerful and beyond my ability to overcome.’

41.word_for_word: saparyām — worship; pūjām — ceremonial honor; sarveṣām bhūtānām āśayāḥ — the inner faculties or hearts of all beings; tāni ālayaḥ nivāsaḥ yasya — he whose dwelling place is all those hearts
41.translation: ‘Saparyā’ means worship or ceremonial honor. The Lord is described as the one whose abode is the inner faculty—the heart—of every living being.

45.word_for_word: nijam karma eva nivardhanam yasya — whose own karma would itself bring about the continuation of its result; tathā-bhūtam api — although this was so; mat-ājñā-puraskāreṇa ānayataḥ — while bringing him back in obedience to my command; te na doṣaḥ — there is no fault for you
45.translation: Although the boy's own karma would ordinarily have continued to produce its destined result, Yama incurs no fault in returning him because he does so in obedience to the Lord's explicit command.

47.word_for_word: vatsa iti — ‘my child’; prādhānyena ekasya sambodhanam — singular address applied chiefly to one of the two; guroḥ niṣkrayaḥ — repayment to the teacher; guru-dakṣiṇā — teacher's fee; yuṣmad-vidhayoḥ guroḥ mama kāmānām madhye kaḥ kāmaḥ avaśiṣyate — for a teacher of disciples like you, what desire could remain unfulfilled?; na kaḥ api — none
47.translation: ‘Vatsa,’ ‘my child,’ is a singular form of address directed chiefly to one of the brothers. ‘The teacher's recompense’ means guru-dakṣiṇā. Their guru says: ‘For a teacher who has disciples such as you, what desire of mine could possibly remain unfulfilled? None at all.’

48.translation: The address is simply, ‘O two heroes.’

49.word_for_word: anila-vat raṃhaḥ vegaḥ yasya tena — with speed like the wind
49.translation: They traveled with speed like that of the wind.

50.word_for_word: parjanyaḥ meghaḥ — a raincloud; tadvat ninadaḥ yasya — whose sound was like thunder; naṣṭam adṛṣṭam tat punaḥ labdha-dhanam yābhiḥ tāḥ iva — like persons who have recovered wealth that had been lost from sight
50.translation: The sound was like the rumbling of a raincloud. The people rejoiced like those who unexpectedly recover treasure that had long been lost from sight.
